course.title: Ultimate DevOps to MLOps Bootcamp
course.tagline: Take one machine learning model all the way to production, and keep it running.
course.description: A project-driven bootcamp for engineers who need to put machine learning models into production and operate them. You build a house price prediction service end to end: trained by a pipeline, packaged into a container, deployed on Kubernetes, monitored in Grafana, scaled by KEDA, and delivered through GitOps with Argo CD. No machine learning background is needed. Comfort on a command line is.
course.author: Gourav Shah
course.audience: DevOps and platform engineers supporting ML workloads, backend engineers moving toward ML infrastructure, and data scientists who want their models to reach production.
course.project_spine: A house price prediction service. One forked repository grown module by module, from raw CSV through to a GitOps-delivered, self-scaling inference service on Kubernetes.
prereq_knowledge: Comfortable working on a command line
Basic Git — clone, commit, push, branch
Able to read Python, though you will not be asked to write much of it
course.prereq_knowledge_md:
- Comfortable working on a command line
- Basic Git — clone, commit, push, branch
- Able to read Python, though you will not be asked to write much of it
- No machine learning background required
- No Kubernetes background required

install.macos: Install Docker Desktop or Rancher Desktop
install.windows: Install Docker Desktop or Rancher Desktop

spine.kind: A forked project repository grown module by module. Modules 2 and 3 add data, features and a trained model. Module 4 adds Dockerfiles and a compose stack. Module 5 adds .github/workflows. Modules 6 to 8 add deployment/kubernetes, deployment/monitoring and the Argo CD application.

lab.setup: Learners fork github.com/mlopsbootcamp/house-price-predictor and work in their own fork throughout, because later modules require write access for CI pipelines and GitOps. A three node KIND cluster is built in Module 6 and reused by Modules 7 and 8 without being torn down.
lab.probe_block:
python --version
uv --version
git --version
docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'
kubectl version --client
kind --version
helm version --short
command -v hey
lab.install_macos:
brew install python@3.11
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
brew install git
Install Docker Desktop or Rancher Desktop
brew install kubectl
brew install kind
brew install helm
brew install hey
lab.install_linux:
sudo apt-get install -y python3.11
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
sudo apt-get install -y git
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo snap install kubectl --classic
go install sigs.k8s.io/kind@latest
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/master/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
sudo snap install hey

modules.label: M1 · The ML Lifecycle and the Project
modules.title: The ML Lifecycle and the Project You Will Build
objectives: Describe the house price prediction problem and why it is framed as a regression task
Walk the end-to-end machine learning lifecycle from raw data through to a served model
Identify which parts of the lifecycle belong to the data scientist and which belong to you
Name the point in the lifecycle where MLOps work actually begins
modules.lab_intent: No lab. Concept module that sets up the project every later module builds on.
modules.deep_dive_intent: How the handover between data science and engineering goes wrong in practice, and what artifacts a good handover contains.

modules.title: Setting up your MLOps Workstation

Get a container runtime working on macOS, Linux or Windows
Fork and clone the project repository, and explain why forking is required here
Run MLflow as a container and reach its interface
Navigate the project layout and explain the split between notebooks and scripts
modules.lab_intent: Install the toolchain, fork and clone the repo, create the Python environment, and bring up MLflow with Docker Compose.
modules.deep_dive_intent: Why uv replaces pip and venv, how MLflow stores runs behind the tracking server, and what to change when moving from a local tracking server to a shared one.
modules.objectives_md:

- Get a container runtime working on macOS, Linux or Windows

modules.label: M3 · From Data to Model
modules.title: From Raw Data to a Trained Model
objectives: Clean a raw dataset and explain what was dropped and why
Build engineered features and save the transformation as a reusable preprocessor
Split data into training and test sets and read X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test correctly
Define algorithm and hyperparameter grids and compare the resulting runs
Track every experiment in MLflow and defend which model won
modules.lab_intent: Run the processing, feature engineering and training scripts, producing a trained model and a preprocessor, with every run logged to MLflow.
modules.deep_dive_intent: Training and inference feature parity — why the preprocessor must be saved rather than reconstructed, and how the two silently drift apart.

- Split data into training and test sets and read X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test correctly

modules.title: Packaging the Model and Serving it with FastAPI
objectives: Explain what a data scientist hands over and what is missing from that handover
Wrap a model in a FastAPI service with request validation
Write a Dockerfile that packages code and model together, ordered for layer caching
Run the API and the web interface together with Docker Compose
Debug a container that builds cleanly but exits on start
modules.lab_intent: Write Dockerfiles for the API and the Streamlit client, build and test each image, then run both as one stack with Compose.
modules.deep_dive_intent: Baked-in models versus loading from a model registry at startup, and what each choice costs you at rollout time.

modules.label: M5 · CI Pipelines with GitHub Actions
modules.title: Building an MLOps CI Pipeline with GitHub Actions
objectives: Read GitHub Actions workflow syntax and explain triggers, jobs and steps
Store registry credentials correctly as a variable and a secret
Build a multi-stage pipeline where each job depends on the one before it
Pass files between jobs using artifacts, since jobs share no filesystem
Explain why an ML pipeline is an ordinary CI pipeline with a different payload
modules.lab_intent: Write a single-job workflow first, wire up Docker Hub credentials, then build the three-stage pipeline from data processing through model training to image publish.
modules.deep_dive_intent: Why a mutable latest tag breaks every downstream system, and how commit-SHA tagging changes the pipeline and the manifests together.

- Store registry credentials correctly as a variable and a secret

modules.label: M6 · Deploying on Kubernetes
modules.title: Deploying the Model on Kubernetes
objectives: Explain why model inference benefits from an orchestrator
Use Pods, Deployments and Services correctly, and say what each one is for
Build a three node KIND cluster and deploy both the model and the frontend
Connect two services by DNS name rather than IP address
Generate manifests instead of writing them, and manage them together with kustomize
modules.lab_intent: Build the cluster, deploy model and frontend with NodePort services, connect them by service name, then replace every command with generated YAML applied through kustomize.
modules.deep_dive_intent: How a Service actually routes to Pods through endpoints and kube-proxy, and what breaks when label selectors do not match.
modules.objectives_md:
- Explain why model inference benefits from an orchestrator

modules.label: M7 · Monitoring and Autoscaling
modules.title: Monitoring and Autoscaling Model Inference
objectives: Separate system monitoring from model monitoring and say which this module covers
Install Prometheus and Grafana with Helm and instrument a FastAPI application
Point Prometheus at your service with a ServiceMonitor and verify data is arriving
Explain why CPU is often the wrong scaling signal for model inference
Scale on a Prometheus query with KEDA, and right-size Pods with a VPA
Run a load test and read the latency distribution rather than the average
modules.lab_intent: Two labs. First install the monitoring stack, instrument the API and build a dashboard. Then install KEDA, scale on latency and request rate, load test it, and add a Vertical Pod Autoscaler.
modules.deep_dive_intent: Reading histogram buckets and histogram_quantile properly, and why an HPA and a VPA acting on the same CPU metric fight each other.
modules.objectives_md:

- Point Prometheus at your service with a ServiceMonitor and verify data is arriving

objectives: Explain why a Deployment cannot protect you from a model that fails quietly

modules.label: M10 · Drift Detection and Retraining
modules.title: Drift Detection and Automated Retraining
objectives: Describe data drift and why every service-level check misses it
Capture a baseline in the transformed feature space and explain why the raw space is wrong

Trigger retraining from evidence rather than from a schedule

modules.lab_intent: Two labs. Instrument the model to score drift against a training baseline and gate releases on it, then close the loop so sustained drift triggers a retrain that flows back through GitOps and the gates.
modules.deep_dive_intent: Training and inference feature parity as a failure class, why the mean of top-K z-scores beats a flat mean, and what the drift signal cannot tell you about why the data changed.
